info.bio:
Jackson Browne - nombre completo Clyde Jackson Browne - (Heidelberg, 9 octubre 1948) es un cantautor estadounidense.

Sus canciones introspectivas y llenas de referencias literarias han hecho de él uno de los más influyentes exponentes de la música de la Costa Oeste de los años 70. 

Brillante cantautor, guitarrista y pianista, con los años se ha hecho famoso también por su compromiso con las causas civiles y con el medio ambiente.

Se le puede comparar con Nick Drake y Neil Young

scenes.name: Cantautores de los setenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: James Taylor se convierte, misteriosamente, en el prototipo del cantautor de los setenta; Carole King, Carly Simon y Don McLean, sobrevalorados. Las innovaciones llegan del oeste: Randy Newman y sus viñetas urbanas con fusión de estilos populares, Shawn Phillips, J.J. Cale y su estilo «laid-back», Gram Parsons, Emmylou Harris, Roger McGuinn, Jackson Browne (Late For The Sky) y, sobre todo, Tom Waits, discípulo de Beefheart y cronista de marginados (Swordfishtrombones, Rain Dogs). Excéntricos como Todd Rundgren y Annette Peacock; en Gran Bretaña, Peter Hammill, Anthony Moore, Richard Thompson, Robert Calvert, John Cale, Kevin Coyne, Elton John y los ex Beatles. El realismo de Bruce Springsteen, verdadero heredero de Woody Guthrie y del blues, y la escuela italiana de cantautores (De André, Guccini, Battisti, Sorrenti).

mentions.text: …melody and tamed rock'n'roll rhythm. Roger McGuinn (1973) and especially Cardiff Rose (1976) defined the classic sound of the post-hippy synthesis. Jackson Browne (4) was far more significant than James Taylor in modernizing the trade. The atmosphere of his first album, Jackson Browne (1972), harks back to sacred hymns not to country-rock ballads, and the arrangements sounded like chamber music for piano, violin and guitar. The religious feeling increased on For Everyman (1973), that introduced his long, tormented meditations on life. podcast.title: Following James Taylor's Path
podcast.body: Jackson Browne is described as having "walked right in" through the door opened by James Taylor's success, benefiting from the momentum of the singer-songwriter movement. He played at The Troubadour and opened for Linda Ronstadt. "And then Jackson Brown just walked right in."

podcast.title: Interpretation of "Werewolves of London"
podcast.body: Jackson Browne offered an alternative interpretation of Warren Zevon's "Werewolves of London," suggesting the song was "more about a ladies man" rather than literally depicting a werewolf, highlighting a deeper, metaphorical meaning. "you might agree with Jackson Brown and say it's more about more of a ladies man."

podcast.title: Live Performance with Roy Orbison
podcast.body: Jackson Browne joined Roy Orbison as a backing singer and musician for his live TV special "A Black and White Night," demonstrating his admiration for Orbison. "He got inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and recorded a live TV special, a black and white night, where he was joined by Elvis's 70s backing band, Bruce Springsteen, Elvis Costello, K.D. Lang, Bunny Raite, Jackson Brown and Tom Wait, among others, while just acting as backing singers and musicians for a man they admired."

podcast.title: Reflection on The Troubadour
podcast.body: Jackson Browne described The Troubadour as an "amazing place, an amazing time," highlighting its role as a crucial showcase for artists on the verge of becoming hugely successful, like Elton John. He also noted its consistent function as a folk club that offered intimate performances for fans and writers, contrasting with occasional large venue shows. "But it was an amazing place, an amazing time because at the same time it was a really important showcase for artists that were about to become huge."
